items.headline: Google gives publishers a new way to fight AI-driven traffic losses
items.facts: Google introduced a “Preferred Sources” button for publishers to let readers mark them as a favorite, aiming to boost traffic as AI search reduces clicks.

framing.narrativeTitle: Google and the Preferred Sources Button
framing.publicBrief: AI tools answer questions without sending clicks to sites. Online publishers are losing traffic fast. Google added a "Preferred Sources" button. Readers can mark a site as a favorite. This tells Google to show that site first. Publishers need readers to care. Google needs readers to trust the tool.

roleFlavor.hunter: You are part of a publishing team. You write stories that people want to read. You need clicks to pay the bills. You hope readers will put your site on their list.

STAG.label: TRUST THE BUTTON
STAG.meaning: Publishers promote the button. Readers use it to mark favorites.
STAG.outcome: Traffic returns to sites. The system works for everyone.

HARE.label: IGNORE THE BUTTON
HARE.meaning: Publishers ignore the tool. Readers keep browsing as usual.
HARE.outcome: AI keeps the clicks. Publishers lose income. The button fails.

howItWorks: Publishers must ask readers to use the new button.
Readers must decide if they will mark sites as favorites.
If both sides try, traffic goes back to the publishers.
If one side waits, the click stream stays with AI tools.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Will you use the Preferred Sources button?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The button works. Readers click. Publishers earn.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side gives up. The button is ignored. Traffic drops.
outcomes.MIXED: Some use it. Some do not. The result is mixed.

items.headline: Mark Zuckerberg bought an Irish castle
items.facts: Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan bought Strancally Castle in Ireland.

framing.publicBrief: Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan bought Strancally Castle in Ireland from a private seller. They paid a price that the seller had asked for, and the deal closed after a short negotiation. The castle is now owned by the Zuckerberg couple.

roleFlavor.proposer: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, the buyers, who have already paid the agreed price
roleFlavor.responder: the seller, who sold the castle for the agreed amount

howItWorks: The buyers offered a price and the seller accepted it. The seller had no other offers. The deal closed once the payment was made. The buyers now own the castle.

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The castle is now owned by Zuckerberg and Chan. The seller receives the money. Both parties are satisfied.

items.headline: How an Indie Studio Convinced ‘Naruto’ Creator, TV Tokyo to Let Them Make Franchise’s First Official
items.facts: Indie studio Sekai secured rights from Naruto creator and TV Tokyo to produce the franchise's first official digital cards app.

framing.narrativeTitle: Sekai Secures Naruto Card App Deal
framing.publicBrief: Sekai, an indie game studio, asked the creator of Naruto and TV Tokyo for permission. The creator and TV Tokyo said yes. Sekai will build the first official digital card app for the series. The studio hopes the app will bring fans together and make money. TV Tokyo hopes the app will keep the brand popular and earn royalties. Both sides must keep their promises for the deal to work.

roleFlavor.proposer: Sekai holds the code and design work for the new app. If the deal falls apart, they lose the chance to launch a first‑ever product.
roleFlavor.responder: TV Tokyo controls the Naruto brand rights. If they back out, they lose a new revenue stream and risk fan disappointment.

howItWorks: Sekai shows the app plan to TV Tokyo. TV Tokyo can accept or reject the plan. Both sides decide at the same time. If TV Tokyo accepts, the app is built and both
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Will TV Tokyo approve the app plan?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: TV Tokyo approves. Sekai builds the app and both enjoy the new product.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: TV Tokyo rejects. Sekai cannot launch the app and loses the opportunity.
outcomes.MIXED: TV Tokyo accepts with changes. Sekai must adjust the app, delaying release.

items.headline: Netflix, AMC Team for ‘Bannerman’ Series Based on John R. Maxim Spy Novels, Shane Black and Craig Si
items.facts: Netflix and AMC Studios agreed to co-produce the drama series 'Bannerman' based on John R. Maxim's novels.

framing.publicBrief: Netflix and AMC Studios have agreed to co-produce the drama series 'Bannerman'. The show is based on John R. Maxim's spy novels. Both companies want the series to succeed. They must share the work and the risks. If one side pulls back, the whole project stalls. They need to trust each other to deliver a hit show.

roleFlavor.contributor: You are a key partner in this new series. Your studio holds half the responsibility. You must commit resources now, hoping the other side does the same.

howItWorks: This is a partnership between Netflix and AMC Studios. Both sides must invest effort and money. You cannot see what the other side is spending right now. If bot
missionCopy.choicePrompt: How much will you invest in 'Bannerman'?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Both studios fully commit. 'Bannerman' becomes a global hit.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One studio holds back. The series falters and loses viewers.
outcomes.MIXED: Uneven effort leads to a mediocre show. No one wins big.

items.headline: 270,000 Square Miles Around Easter Island to Become Indigenous-Managed Ocean Reserve
items.facts: Indigenous people of Easter Island will hold a voting majority on a sea council governing a new marine protected area, with 6 seats versus 5 for Chilean officials.

framing.publicBrief: A large ocean area near Easter Island is becoming a protected zone. A new council will manage it. The Indigenous people of Easter Island hold six seats on this council. Chilean officials hold five seats. The Indigenous group has a voting majority. They must decide how to run the reserve together. The sea is vast and dark tonight. The council meets in the quiet. Every vote counts for the future of the water.

roleFlavor.contributor: You sit on the council. You have a vote. You care for the sea.

howItWorks: You are part of the sea council.
The Indigenous people hold six seats.
Chilean officials hold five seats.
Decisions require group agreement.

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The council agrees on a plan.

items.headline: How an Indie Studio Convinced ‘Naruto’ Creator, TV Tokyo to Let Them Make Franchise’s First Licensed
items.facts: Sekai negotiated with the Naruto creator and TV Tokyo to secure rights for a digital card game.

framing.narrativeTitle: Sekai Secures Naruto Card Game Deal
framing.publicBrief: Sekai sat down with the creator of Naruto and TV Tokyo. They talked about making a digital card game using the Naruto name. Sekai wants to launch the game and earn fans. The creator and TV Tokyo want to protect the brand and earn money from the deal. Both sides must decide what terms to accept.

roleFlavor.proposer: Sekai hopes the game will bring new fans and revenue.
roleFlavor.responder: The Naruto creator and TV Tokyo guard the brand and look for a fair share.

howItWorks: Sekai offers a contract with payment and creative control details.
The creator and TV Tokyo review the offer and can ask for changes.
Both sides see each other's proposals at the same time.
If they agree, the card game can be released. If not, the deal falls apart.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Choose the final terms of the agreement

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The contract is signed. The game launches and both parties share the profits.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side pulls out. The game never launches and both lose potential earnings.
outcomes.MIXED: They reach a partial agreement. The game launches with limited features, giving modest returns to both.

items.headline: Travelodge CEO Exits After Mishandling of Guest’s Sexual Assault Case
items.facts: Travelodge CEO Jo Boydell resigned after pressure over the group’s handling of a sexual assault case.

framing.narrativeTitle: Jo Boydell Steps Down from Travelodge
framing.publicBrief: Travelodge group faces a storm after a guest reported sexual assault. The case drew angry headlines. Stakeholders in the hotel industry press the chain for a clear response. Jo Boydell, the chief executive, steps down as pressure mounts. The group must decide how to rebuild trust while the industry watches.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are Jo Boydell, the departing CEO, holding the power to shape the company’s next move.
roleFlavor.responder: You are the industry stakeholders, watching Travelodge and ready to judge its actions.

howItWorks: Each side makes a single offer.
The other side can accept or reject it.
If the offer is accepted, the deal goes through.
If it is rejected, both sides walk away.

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Travelodge and the industry agree on a plan, restoring confidence.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side refuses the other's terms, deepening the crisis.
outcomes.MIXED: A partial agreement is reached, leaving some issues unresolved.

items.headline: FCC officially decides gigabit speeds are too good for you
items.facts: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr decided to cancel long‑term broadband speed goals, ending the push for gigabit downloads.

framing.publicBrief: It is evening at the Federal Communications Commission. Chairman Brendan Carr has made his decision. He cancels the long-term goal for gigabit broadband speeds. This ends the push for faster internet access for all Americans. The telecom industry supports this move. They do not want strict speed targets. The public loses a promise of better service. The deal is final. The rules are gone.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. You hold the power to set national rules. You can choose to keep the speed goals or cancel them. Your choice ends the debate.
roleFlavor.responder: You represent the telecom industry. You want no strict speed targets. You prefer to set your own pace for upgrades. You accept the cancellation as a win.

howItWorks: Brendan Carr makes the final decision on broadband goals.
The telecom industry reacts to his choice.
If he keeps the goals, the industry must comply.
If he cancels them, the industry is free to act.

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Goals kept. Industry complies. Public gets faster internet promises.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Goals cancelled. Industry wins. Public loses the promise of speed.
outcomes.MIXED: Partial deal. Some goals remain. Industry faces some rules.

items.headline: How Florida quietly removed climate change content from textbooks
items.facts: Florida state requested publishers to dilute climate change content; publishers complied, altering textbook language.

framing.narrativeTitle: Florida State and Publishers Swap Words on Climate
framing.publicBrief: Florida state asked publishers to soften climate change talk in school books. Publishers changed the words to meet the request. The state keeps the new text, the publishers keep the rest of the book.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are Florida state. You want the books to say less about climate change.
roleFlavor.responder: You are Publishers. You want to keep the original words but must obey the state.

howItWorks: Florida state tells publishers what to say in the books.
Publishers can choose to follow the request or refuse.
If they follow, the books change and Florida keeps the new text.
If they refuse, the books stay the same but Florida may act against them.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Will the publishers change the words?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Publishers changed the words. Florida keeps the new text.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Publishers kept the original words. Florida may act against them.
outcomes.MIXED: Publishers partially changed the words. Florida keeps the new text.

items.headline: The Dinner Party Has Left the Building
items.facts: Artists created a dinner setting on a natural rock by a waterfall and invited diners to eat there.

framing.publicBrief: Charles Michel set a table on a rock by a waterfall. He invited diners to eat there. The water rushes around the stone. The air is cool and wet. It is night. The table is ready. The food is hot. The diners must decide if they will come. They can stay home for safety. Or they can join him for the meal. The lights are low. The sound of water is loud.

roleFlavor.hunter: You are part of the group invited to eat. You hold your place at the table. You risk the wet rocks. You see the fire and the food if you come.

STAG.label: JOIN THE MEAL
STAG.meaning: Walk to the rock and sit down.
STAG.outcome: You eat the feast together. The night is a success.

HARE.label: STAY HOME
HARE.outcome: You stay dry and safe. The table remains empty.

howItWorks: Both guests choose at the same time. Neither can see the other. If both join, the party happens. If both stay, nothing happens.
If one joins and the other stays, the guest who joins is left alone. The guest who stays is safe but misses out. Coming together gives the best result.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Will you sit at the table?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The feast is shared. Everyone eats well.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One person is alone in the dark. The other is safe.
outcomes.MIXED: The table is empty. The food goes cold.
